interactions.label: Which pattern of nasal obstruction most strongly suggests a structural cause suc

params.question: Which pattern of nasal obstruction most strongly suggests a structural cause such as deviated nasal septum rather than mucosal inflammatory disease?

answers.text: Bilateral obstruction that worsens with changes in weather

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Bilateral obstruction triggered by environmental changes is typical of mucosal inflammatory conditions such as allergic or vasomotor rhinitis, not structural disease.

answers.text: Constant unilateral obstruction that is progressively worsening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Constant unilateral obstruction that progresses is the hallmark of structural causes. Laterality is the single most powerful discriminator in evaluating nasal obstruction.

answers.text: Alternating nasal obstruction with profuse watery discharge

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alternating obstruction with watery discharge points to mucosal inflammatory disease such as allergic rhinitis, which is typically bilateral and variable.
Response to antihistamines indicates a histamine-mediated allergic process — mucosal inflammatory, not structural.

overallFeedback.feedback: Unilateral, constant, progressive obstruction is the classic structural pattern. Bilateral and variable obstruction more commonly reflects mucosal inflammatory disease such as allergic rhinitis.
Exactly right. Laterality is the single most powerful discriminator: unilateral, constant, progressive obstruction demands evaluation for structural or neoplastic causes.

interactions.label: Which of the following symptoms of allergic rhinitis is driven by the late-phase

params.question: Which of the following symptoms of allergic rhinitis is driven by the late-phase leukotriene-mediated eosinophilic response rather than the early histamine-mediated phase?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rhinorrhoea is an early-phase symptom caused by histamine acting on H1 receptors to stimulate glandular hypersecretion within minutes of allergen exposure.
Sneezing is triggered in the early phase when histamine stimulates trigeminal nerve endings in the nasal mucosa.

Correct. Nasal obstruction results from the late-phase response at four to eight hours, where cysteinyl leukotrienes recruit eosinophils, causing persistent turbinate oedema. This is why intranasal corticosteroids, not antihistamines, are needed to control congestion.
Itch is an early-phase symptom mediated by histamine stimulating trigeminal sensory nerve endings — the same mechanism that drives sneezing.

overallFeedback.feedback: Rhinorrhoea, sneezing, and itch are early-phase histamine-mediated symptoms. Persistent nasal obstruction is the fourth cardinal symptom, driven by the late-phase leukotriene–eosinophil response at four to eight hours.
Well done. Persistent nasal obstruction is the late-phase symptom driven by eosinophilic infiltration, and it responds to intranasal corticosteroids rather than antihistamines.

interactions.label: A 25-year-old with moderate–severe persistent allergic rhinitis remains symptoma

params.question: A 25-year-old with moderate–severe persistent allergic rhinitis remains symptomatic despite regular intranasal corticosteroids and oral cetirizine. Which is the most appropriate next step to achieve long-term disease modification?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Allergen immunotherapy is the only disease-modifying treatment for allergic rhinitis. All other drugs — corticosteroids, antihistamines, leukotriene antagonists — provide symptom control without altering the underlying immune response.

answers.text: Switch to oral chlorpheniramine for stronger antihistamine effect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: First-generation antihistamines like chlorpheniramine cross the blood–brain barrier and impair cognition. They are not recommended, and switching antihistamines does not modify the underlying disease.
Ipratropium is an anticholinergic that blocks glandular secretion. It is indicated for rhinorrhoea-dominant vasomotor rhinitis, not for refractory allergic rhinitis.

answers.text: Prescribe a two-week course of oral antibiotics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antibiotics have no role in allergic rhinitis. Yellow-green nasal discharge during a viral illness is neutrophilic debris, not evidence of bacterial infection requiring antibiotics.

overallFeedback.feedback: When maximal pharmacotherapy fails, allergen-specific immunotherapy is the next step. It is the only disease-modifying option; corticosteroids and antihistamines control symptoms but do not alter the underlying immune response.
Exactly right. Allergen immunotherapy is the only treatment that modifies the disease course in allergic rhinitis — everything else is symptom control.

interactions.label: In the first-aid management of epistaxis, the patient should tilt the head backw

params.question: In the first-aid management of epistaxis, the patient should tilt the head backward to prevent blood from dripping out of the nose.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Tilting the head back is a common misconception. It directs blood posteriorly into the pharynx and airway, risking aspiration. The correct first-aid measure is sitting the patient forward while pinching the soft, cartilaginous nose firmly for fifteen minutes.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Well identified. Tilting the head back directs blood into the oropharynx and airway, risking aspiration. The correct position is sitting the patient forward and pinching the soft, cartilaginous part of the nose firmly for fifteen minutes.

metadata.title: In the first-aid management of epistaxis

interactions.label: A polysomnography report shows 25 apnoea–hypopnoea events per hour. Which severi

params.question: A polysomnography report shows 25 apnoea–hypopnoea events per hour. Which severity classification and first-line treatment is correct?

answers.text: Mild obstructive sleep apnoea; positional therapy and weight loss alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mild OSA is defined as 5–15 events per hour. Twenty-five events per hour exceeds this threshold and requires more definitive intervention.
Severe OSA is defined as more than 30 events per hour. At 25 events per hour the disease is moderate, and CPAP — not surgery — is the first-line treatment.

answers.text: Moderate obstructive sleep apnoea; oral antihistamines and nasal decongestants

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antihistamines and decongestants do not address the pharyngeal collapse that causes OSA. Moderate–severe disease requires CPAP to maintain airway patency during sleep.

answers.text: Moderate obstructive sleep apnoea; continuous positive airway pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An AHI of 15–30 is classified as moderate obstructive sleep apnoea. CPAP is the first-line treatment for moderate to severe disease, supplemented by weight loss as the single most effective modifiable intervention.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Apnoea–Hypopnoea Index classifies OSA as mild (5–15), moderate (15–30), or severe (above 30). At 25 events per hour this is moderate, and CPAP is the first-line treatment for moderate to severe disease.
Well done. An AHI of 25 places this in the moderate range, where CPAP combined with weight loss is the standard of care.
